clue.text: Like this clue, a mixture

blocks.note: taken as written
a cross is a hybrid, a mixture of two breeds

explanation.surface: A setter teasingly describes their own clue as something of a jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: it sits in the across half of the grid, and A CROSS read as one word gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues are listed under two headings, and this one belongs to the horizontal set, so it is literally one of those entries.

clue.text: What could be caught on Lahore trip?

definitions.text: What could be caught on Lahore trip?

indicators.note: a trip can mean a stumble, so the city's name falls over into a new order

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the six letters of the Pakistani city, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller to Pakistan worries about which illness they might pick up on the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a disease one might catch on a trip to Lahore, built from C plus the city's letters jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an infectious intestinal disease contracted from contaminated water, a real risk for travellers in South Asia.

clue.text: More than a jolly style of delivery

blocks.note: over means in excess of
taken as written
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone describes a delivery style that is rather more than merely cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Jolly looks like an adjective but is a noun here: a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler delivers the ball overarm, with the arm swung above the shoulder, as the law requires.

clue.text: Continue to rise and fall as performer in theatre

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: to keep heaving like the sea
second meaning: one who operates in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: An actor's career keeps going up and down on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre suggests a stage actor, but the theatre is a hospital's operating room. The first meaning splits the word into SURGE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical specialist who carries out operations works in the operating theatre, the 'performance' being the procedure itself.

clue.text: Put an end to call for strike

blocks.note: to stop is to bring to a halt
to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager

explanation.surface: A union leader announces an end to the call for industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work by employees as a protest, which is what an industrial strike amounts to.

clue.text: Play patience

blocks.note: first meaning: the permitted slack or variation in a machine part
second meaning: forbearance towards others

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like an instruction to play the card game patience (solitaire); both words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers speak of the allowed margin of error in a part as its play, and forbearance toward others is the everyday sense.

clue.text: Consumed and enjoyed

blocks.note: first meaning: wholly gripped by a feeling or a spirit
second meaning: had or owned, as one enjoys a privilege

explanation.surface: Someone describes a meal they ate and liked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests eating a meal; consumed means gripped, as by jealousy, and enjoyed means owned, as in enjoying good health.
explanation.definitionFit: One consumed by rage is held by it as if by a demon, and to enjoy a right is to have it in one's ownership.

clue.text: There are bodies in his study

definitions.text: There are bodies in his study

blocks.clueFragment: There are bodies in his study
blocks.note: surface reading: corpses found in someone's study, like a murder mystery
setter's reading: the subject this man studies is the structure of the body

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a detective story with corpses in a library; study is the man's field of research.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist examines the structure of living things, traditionally by dissecting cadavers, so corpses are literally his subject.

clue.text: Sort of college where one gets to choose exam

blocks.note: to elect is to choose by vote
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A university is described as letting students pick their own examination.
explanation.walkthrough: Sort of college invites thoughts of a university; it is the American body that formally chooses the president.
explanation.definitionFit: The US electoral college is the assembly of representatives that casts the votes choosing the president.

clue.text: Nod off — it's almost twelve

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for the number falls one letter short

blocks.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: Someone drifts off to sleep as midnight approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve suggests the clock striking; it is the number a dozen, missing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to sleep lightly, the same brief drifting-off that nodding off describes.

clue.text: Property of extremely rare beer, say

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outermost letters of the next word count

blocks.note: the first and last letters of rare
ale is a kind of beer
to say is to state

explanation.surface: Someone praises the quality of a particularly scarce beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Property looks like a quality of the beer; it is the definition, land and buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is the standard term, especially in America, for land and the buildings on it held as property.

clue.text: Went off, we hear, for the duration of the Trojan war

definitions.text: the duration of the Trojan war

indicators.note: we hear points to the sound of a word rather than how it is written

blocks.note: food that went off has rotted

explanation.surface: Something rotted over the long years the Greeks spent besieging Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend the siege of Troy lasted ten years.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of ten years is exactly how long Homer's siege of Troy lasted, so the definition is a classical way of saying that span.

clue.text: Open the sack and plunder

blocks.note: to free something is to open it up or release it
getting the boot means getting the sack, being dismissed

explanation.surface: A looter unties a bag and helps themselves to its contents.
explanation.walkthrough: The sack looks like a bag to open; it is dismissal from a job, which is also the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A freebooter is a pirate, and to act as one is to go raiding and pillaging for loot.

clue.text: Game providing poor source of revenue given no backing

indicators.note: backing suggests moving backwards, so the short word is read from its end

blocks.note: poor quality is bad
the Mint makes money, a source of revenue
the word no, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sport is dismissed as a poor earner because nobody will sponsor it.
explanation.walkthrough: Given no backing looks like a lack of sponsors; backing reverses the word no.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net, a common type of competitive game.

clue.text: Where directors decide to add love in Shakespeare play

indicators.note: add tells us a further letter is put into what follows
in places that letter inside the following words

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, a round O
the Bard is Shakespeare's familiar title
play is room to move, as in a loose joint

explanation.surface: Executives settle on staging a romantic comedy by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare play suggests a title such as Love's Labour's Lost; it is two pieces, the Bard and a word for space to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Company directors meet and take decisions in this room, where the board convenes around a table.

clue.text: Topsy-turvy list seen in primer

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, so in a down clue the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rota is a list of duties
something noted has been seen

explanation.surface: A jumbled list appears in a beginners' textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Primer suggests a children's reading book; here it is the charge that sets off an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is the small charge or cap used to ignite a main explosive, which is just what a detonator does.

clue.text: Appliance foolish chaps fail to start on time

indicators.note: failing to start means the opening is lost, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: simple men are foolish chaps
t is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A household gadget is blamed on silly men who cannot get it going on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Foolish chaps gives SIMPLE MEN, which loses its S before T is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a tool or piece of equipment used for a job, much as an appliance is a device put to a purpose.

clue.text: Female and Rex go separately into bar, for change

indicators.note: going into puts the two letters inside, and separately means at different points

blocks.note: a transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door
f is the abbreviation for female
R stands for Rex, king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A woman and a man called Rex arrive at a pub separately, wanting a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar suggests a pub; it is a structural crossbar. The F goes in after TRANS and the R after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to alter completely, so the verb change is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One going downhill shot in the air

blocks.note: first meaning: someone descending a slope on skis
second meaning: a cricket stroke that sends the ball high up

explanation.surface: A person on the slopes is hit by gunfire overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a skier is a ball hit steeply upwards, usually an easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skiing descends the mountain, and the cricketing term is a mishit sending the ball up toward the sky.

clue.text: Misbehave in court after serve

indicators.note: after places the courtroom phrase second, following the word for serve

blocks.note: to serve as something is to act as it
someone up before the judge is in court

explanation.surface: A tennis player throws a tantrum on court after serving.
explanation.walkthrough: Court and serve paint a tennis match, but the court is a law court, where a defendant is said to be up before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is an informal phrasal verb for behaving badly or causing trouble, as a naughty child does.

clue.text: Moving tale can do as a story

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts them into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A touching story turns out to work perfectly well as a narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving looks like touching, praise for the tale; it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that is told as personal accounts rather than measured facts is described by this adjective, meaning in the form of a story.

clue.text: Secret's out — this'll shed some light

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put out of place

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the secret is out, the truth will be illuminated.
explanation.walkthrough: A cresset is an old iron basket holding burning fuel, used as a torch or beacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is a metal container of burning oil or coal mounted as a lamp, so it literally gives out light.

clue.text: Actually in progress when it's time to say goodbye

definitions.text: when it's time to say goodbye

blocks.note: first meaning: continuing at present

blocks.clueFragment: when it's time to say goodbye
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: at the moment of departure

explanation.surface: A farewell is already happening at the moment of parting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word as ON GOING, at the point of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still under way is continuing, while 'on going' means upon one's departure, the moment for farewells.

clue.text: Use excessive flattery? That's extremely unusual in a social companion

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outer letters of the next word are kept
in places those letters inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the first and last letters of unusual
taken as written
a date is someone you go out with

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that heaping praise on a dinner partner is very odd behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to praise or admire someone fawningly and beyond what is due, which is overdoing flattery.

clue.text: Parisian tripper, originally Sudanese

indicators.note: originally says these letters were once in another form before being rearranged

blocks.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist in Paris turns out to have come from Sudan.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripper looks like a tourist; it is one who trips lightly, a dancer, and the French word makes her Parisian.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseuse is the French word for a female ballet dancer, someone who trips the light fantastic on stage.

clue.text: It provides support as soldiers go in after breakthrough

definitions.text: It provides support as soldiers go in after breakthrough

blocks.clueFragment: It provides support as soldiers go in after breakthrough
blocks.note: surface reading: military backup as troops advance through a breached line
setter's reading: strips of toast are dipped in once the shell is cracked open at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain soldiers are narrow strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg; the breakthrough is cracking the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: This small holder keeps a boiled egg upright at the table while the diner dips toast fingers into the yolk.

clue.text: Lacking cash, when ordering drinks, it might be said

definitions.text: when ordering drinks, it might be said

blocks.note: first meaning: broke, in financial ruin

blocks.clueFragment: when ordering drinks, it might be said
blocks.note: second meaning: what a customer says asking for a drink served over ice

explanation.surface: A customer at a bar realises they are short of money as they order.
explanation.definitionFit: A failed business or person with no money is said to be ruined like a wrecked ship, and a spirit poured over ice is served this way.

clue.text: Sort of vehicle used by single man

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a van is a kind of vehicle

explanation.surface: A bachelor drives a particular kind of vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Single man suggests a bachelor; man alone is the definition, and single gives the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a common Russian male first name, and crosswords often define first names simply as a man.

clue.text: Naval force retreating one hour later

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: to ram is to force
I is the Roman numeral one
the hour is the time of day

explanation.surface: A navy squadron withdraws an hour late.
explanation.walkthrough: Naval force looks like a fleet; Naval alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things relating to the sea and shipping, close to naval though wider than warships alone.

clue.text: Doubly good-hearted cat in children's stories

indicators.note: hearted puts a letter at the heart, the middle of the word that follows

blocks.note: a tiger is a big cat
g for good, added beside the one already at the centre so it appears twice

explanation.surface: A storybook cat is described as twice as kind as most.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding G to the middle of TIGER doubles its central letter. The word cat does double duty, in both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger is the bouncy tiger friend of Winnie-the-Pooh in A. A. Milne's books for young readers.
